clue.text: Dismal time on regularly uphill journey

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the first pieces follow the alternate letters
regularly says take every other letter of the word uphill

parts.note: dismal means grim
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A gloomy stretch spent trudging steadily uphill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks letters two, four and six of uphill; 'on' in an across clue means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a journey made to a sacred place.

clue.text: Record briefly over final bit of The Crown

indicators.note: in a down clue, over says the shortened word is turned upside down, read backwards
briefly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to tape something is to record it

indicators.note: final bit of takes the last letter of the word The

explanation.surface: Seems to tell you to note the closing moment of the TV series The Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts TAPE to TAP; 'over' turns it to PAT; then E, the end of The. 'The Crown' looks like the TV drama, but only 'Crown' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Pate is an old word for the head, especially its top, which is also called the crown.

clue.text: Small type of cow maybe squashing bag

parts.note: a cow is one example of an animal that lows, so a lower
a case is a bag for carrying things

explanation.surface: A small breed of cow crushing a bag underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squashing' just links the two pieces placed side by side; LOWER reads as 'one that moos', not the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower case letters are the small letters of a typeface, as against capitals.

clue.text: Part of squirrel iconised as something holy

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A squirrel turned into a religious icon, revered as sacred.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object revered for its link to a saint, a holy thing.

clue.text: Thousands surrounding yard soon toppled Greek place

indicators.note: surrounding says the thousands go round the yard

parts.note: M and K are both abbreviations for a thousand

indicators.note: toppled says the letters of soon are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Large numbers ringing a yard that will shortly collapse somewhere in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: Both M and K stand for thousand, hence the plural; 'surrounding' and the anagram signal 'toppled' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mykonos is an island in the Greek Cyclades, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Gay mates both extremely on edge in school dress

indicators.note: both extremely takes the first and last letters of each of the two words

parts.note: a lip is the edge of a cup or crater

explanation.surface: Cheerful friends nervously wearing school uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both extremely' takes the outer letters of each word; 'on edge' reads as nervous but splits into a link and a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymslip is a sleeveless tunic once worn by British schoolgirls as uniform.

clue.text: Prevent loads of dosh being returned

indicators.note: being returned says the word is read backwards

parts.note: pots of money means a great deal of it; dosh is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Stop a big pile of cash being given back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being returned' turns POTS round.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something is to prevent it happening.

clue.text: Tattooist uses the ten inks originally all at once

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of each word that follows it

explanation.surface: A tattoo artist works with ten different inks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' picks the initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is a musical direction meaning every performer plays together.

clue.text: Adult in silent pic possibly is modelling material

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: An adult appears in an old silent film, perhaps as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A with SILENTPIC; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasticine is a soft modelling clay used by children and animators.

clue.text: Come in to support fool who might agree to all sorts

definitions.text: who might agree to all sorts

indicators.note: in a down clue, the supporting word sits below the other

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to enter is to come in

explanation.surface: Come in to back a fool who will say yes to anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts ENTER below ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: An assenter is someone who agrees, a yes-man.

clue.text: Digger that hasn't run dry

indicators.note: that hasn't says the digger lacks the following letter

parts.note: a trowel is a small hand tool for digging
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A dig at a digger that has failed to dry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that hasn't' removes R from TROWEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To towel something is to rub it dry with cloth.

clue.text: Trauma as king misinterpreted manual?

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: misinterpreted says the letters are read wrongly, put into another order

explanation.surface: A king misreads trauma as something else in an instruction book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misinterpreted' rearranges TRAUMA AS into AMASUTRA, after K.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kama Sutra is an ancient Indian guide to love, a famous handbook; the question mark admits the cheek.

clue.text: Drug half of elephant's biscuit

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine

indicators.note: half of takes the first three of the six letters

parts.note: Nellie the Elephant is a British children's song, so Nellie is a byname for an elephant

explanation.surface: Some drug, half meant for an elephant, in a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps NEL from NELLIE, from the British song Nellie the Elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cracknel is a light crisp biscuit.

clue.text: Fish put back by court order

indicators.note: put back says the fish's name is read backwards

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Return a fish next to a court ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns IDE into EDI; 'by' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official order or decree.

clue.text: One who checks tanks before going to bed?

definitions.text: One who checks tanks before going to bed?

parts.words: One who checks tanks before going to bed?
parts.note: the bed is the seabed, and the tanks hold air for breathing underwater

explanation.walkthrough: The picture is someone at home checking the water tanks before sleep; the bed is the ocean floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver using breathing apparatus checks their air cylinders before descending to the sea floor.

clue.text: Leaves to collect seaweed for fuel

indicators.note: to collect says the lettuce gathers the seaweed inside it

parts.note: cos is a lettuce, eaten for its leaves
a seaweed is an alga

explanation.surface: Foliage gathering seaweed to burn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, departs; it is the lettuce. 'to collect' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal gas, made by heating coal, was once the main domestic gas supply.

clue.text: Moving target essentially for kite flyer

indicators.note: moving says the letters of target are shifted about
essentially takes the heart of the word kite

explanation.surface: A moving target is basically what a kite flyer has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges TARGET as GREAT; 'essentially' takes IT from kite. 'kite flyer' reads as one phrase but 'flyer' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The great tit is a common European songbird, so a bird that flies.

clue.text: River flower near to river from the east

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Po is the Italian river

indicators.note: in an across clue, from the east means read right to left

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A river bloom found by the waterside, heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows, the Po; 'from the east' turns CAM; 'near' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac is the river flowing past Washington DC.

clue.text: Revolution of island capital master easily recollected

indicators.note: revolution of says the pieces are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Elba is a Mediterranean island
Rome is the Italian capital
M is short for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: An uprising on an island leading to the capital's master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution of' reverses ELBAROMEM; Elba links to Napoleon, a joke on revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Something memorable is worth remembering and so easily recalled.

clue.text: Ale experts better after draining jugs

indicators.note: after draining leaves only the outside letters, the inside emptied

parts.note: ewers are large water jugs

explanation.surface: Beer specialists do better once they've emptied their jugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after draining' empties better to BR.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewers make beer, so they are the specialists in ale.

clue.text: Lay copper end of spool inside special organ

indicators.note: inside says the copper and letter go within the organ

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of spool

explanation.surface: A police officer lays down the end of a reel in a special instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb but is the adjective; 'inside' puts CUL within EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay means not of the clergy, which is what secular means.

clue.text: In favour of recalling title "Gaffer"

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: recalling, calling back, says the word is read backwards

parts.note: a name is a title

explanation.surface: Supporting a nickname for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalling' means calling back, so the word for title is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is British slang for the boss or overseer, the foreman.

clue.text: Partner initially is actually not coping in charge

indicators.note: in says the initials go inside the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A spouse-to-be who is actually struggling to cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' covers the four words after it; 'in charge' looks like one phrase but 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiancée is a woman engaged to be married, a partner.

clue.text: Crockery gift maker stored in empty depot

indicators.note: stored in says the gift maker is kept within
empty removes the inside, leaving the outer letters of depot

parts.note: Santa's elves make the Christmas presents

explanation.surface: Pottery presents kept in an empty warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves only the outer letters of depot; 'gift maker' is one of Santa's helpers, kept inside by 'stored in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue and white glazed earthenware from the Dutch town of Delft.

clue.text: Relief from dispute likely in recession

indicators.note: in recession says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Respite from an argument expected during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes PUTEL out of 'dispute likely' and 'in recession' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or easing, a relief from pressure.

clue.text: Former pugilist with additional Highland weapon

parts.note: Cassius Clay was Muhammad Ali's name before he changed it
more means additional

explanation.surface: An ex-boxer carrying an extra Scottish blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is the large two-edged broadsword of the Scottish Highlanders.

clue.text: Figure of 8 dance upset husband

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: a prom is a school dance

explanation.surface: A skater's figure of eight ruins a dance for a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure of 8' looks like a skating shape but points to 8 down, PLASTICINE; 'upset' reverses PROM.
explanation.definitionFit: Morph is a small animated character modelled from Plasticine on British children's TV.

clue.text: Britain avoiding extra responsibility

indicators.note: avoiding says the letter for Britain is left out

parts.note: a bonus is something extra

explanation.surface: Britain dodging extra duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops B from BONUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The onus is the burden or duty of doing something.

clue.text: Terribly civil about threesome? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: about says the anagram goes round the threesome
terribly says the letters of civil are badly arranged

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: Being awfully polite to a group of three, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' signals the anagram and 'about' the container. The definition looks back over the clue: vitriolic is the opposite of civil.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriolic means bitterly abusive, the reverse of being polite.

clue.text: Nick at home being a crime fighter

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal, to rob
in means at home

explanation.surface: A burglar caught at home is a crime fighter after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like police slang or a name; it is the verb to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin is Batman's sidekick in the comics, fighting crime in Gotham.

clue.text: Hunter leaving gold to be transported

indicators.note: leaving says the gold departs from the hunter

parts.note: a raptor is a bird of prey, a hunter
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A hunter abandons the gold to be carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes OR out of RAPTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt and transported both mean carried away with delight.

clue.text: Shoes given away across western coasts

indicators.note: across says the two words lie either side of the western letter

parts.note: something given away is free
heels are high-heeled shoes

explanation.surface: Free footwear handed out along western shores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coasts' looks like a noun, shores; it is the verb, rolling without power. 'across' straddles W.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist freewheels by rolling on without pedalling, which is to coast.
